newsitem.title: USA: baseball-Florida Marlins seek mascot's missing head.
newsitem.headline: baseball-Florida Marlins seek mascot's missing head.

text.p: The Florida Marlins mascot has lost his head and the baseball team wants it back.

The head of Billy the Marlin -- a Disneyesque creature with a long, pointed bill -- was snatched from the grasp of a U.S. Navy SEAL by a gust of wind Tuesday as he parachuted into Pro Player Stadium for the Marlins' opening day ceremony.

The elite soldier, dressed as Billy, had the head strapped to his body, ready to don in mid-flight for his descent into the stadium as part of a SEAL jump team. But as he jumped from the plane, a gust of wind caught the head and ripped it away. It tumbled about 6,000 feet (1,800 metres) and landed -- somewhere.
"The head is still missing," Marlins director of in-game entertainment Susan Budd said Thursday.

"That is a really unruly head," Lou Langlais, a member of the SEALS jump team, told the Miami Herald. "It's too big. It catches too much air in that big, huge mouth. It isn't meant for jumping out of airplanes."
The Marlins offered a reward. South Florida radio stations did the same. Hundreds joined the search and local media reported children and adults were scouring neighbourhoods near the stadium.
The SEAL who lost the head had the presence of mind to land outside the stadium rather than upset children by parachuting headless onto the field.
"Two season tickets if it comes back as smoked Marlin dip (the head in pieces)," Budd said of the club's reward offer. "Four seasons tickets if the whole head is intact."

Billy's loss did not stop him from performing during opening day -- the mascot had a spare. "We want the kids out there to know the real Billy is doing great," Budd said. "He got a new set of clothes."
The Herald said it had set up a toll free hotline for information on the missing head: 1-800-Oh-My-God-There's-A-Beheaded-Mascot-In-My-Pool.
